book

noun
uk
/bʊk/ us
/bʊk/

TEXT

Add to word list Add to word list
A1 [ C ]
a written text that can be published in printed or electronic form
libro
Have you read any good books recently? ¿Ha leído algún buen libro últimamente?
He has a new book out (= published). Ha sacado un nuevo libro.
She wrote a book on car maintenance. Escribió un libro sobre mantenimiento del automóvil.
A1 [ C ]
a set of pages that have been fastened together inside a cover to be read or written in
libro, cuaderno
a hardback/paperback book un libro de tapa dura, un libro de tapa blanda
I took a book with me to read on the plane. Me llevé un libro para leerlo en el avión.
He writes all his expenses in a little book he carries with him. Anota todos sus gastos en un pequeño cuaderno que lleva encima.
[ C ]
one of the parts that a very long book, such as the Bible, is divided into
libro
the book of Job el libro de Job
More examplesFewer examples
  • We're reading a different book this week.
  • In the last two years the book has only sold 200 copies.
  • She published a book of poems and followed it up with a novel.
  • I have to return my library books on the sixth of July.
  • He's the author of several hugely successful children's books .

Idioms

in my book
off the books

book

verb
uk
/bʊk/ us
/bʊk/

ARRANGE

A2 [ T or I ]
to arrange to have a seat, room, performer, etc. at a particular time in the future
reservar, hacer una reserva
[ + two objects ] I've booked us two tickets to see "Carmen"/I've booked two tickets for us to see "Carmen". He reservado dos entradas para ver "Carmen".
She'd booked a table for four at their favourite restaurant. Había reservado una mesa para cuatro en su restaurante favorito.
Will booked a seat on the evening flight to Los Angeles. Will reservó un asiento en el vuelo vespertino a Los Ángeles.
We were advised to book early if we wanted to get a room. Nos aconsejaron que reserváramos pronto si queríamos conseguir una habitación.
They booked a jazz band for their wedding. Contrataron una banda de jazz para su boda.
The hotel/restaurant/theatre is fully booked (up) (= all the rooms/tables/tickets have been taken). El hotel/restaurante/teatro está al completo.
I'd like to go but I'm booked up (= I have arranged to do other things) until the weekend. Me gustaría ir, pero estoy ocupado hasta el fin de semana.
More examplesFewer examples
  • I've booked the car into the garage.
  • I've booked a table at the restaurant for nine o'clock.
  • He booked a double room.
  • We booked the holiday on a whim.
  • It's a good thing that we booked our tickets early.
